# PROCESS — cand_0003 (iteration 3/3)

## Environment faults (handed back, NOT edited for)
- 227-40, 45635: `trace` empty (0 agent turns), the same sandbox `/execute` HTTP 500 that cand_0002 diagnosed. 2/40 tasks. A human must check that the sandbox execute service is stable. No prompt edit was made on their account.

## Ranked issue list
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | lever |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | I. column letters counted rather than read (off by one) | 43436 (1 trial, 0 → 1 recoverable) | Turn 2 comment: "Column J: Open by of end of May 2022 / Column K: Jun". The real layout is H=today, I=May, J=Jun, K=Jul. The agent printed headers as a positional list and counted. It wrote the May/Jun counts into J/K, left I empty and never did Jul. Its own Phase-2 printout `Row 2: I=None, J=1, K=2` contradicted its belief that I was "already filled", and it then re-sent the identical block 5 times. | KNOWLEDGE (method) + STRUCTURE (verify item) | §3 conditional bullet + idiom; Phase 3 checklist item with diagnosis |
| — | ENV | 227-40, 45635 | sandbox 500 | ENV | none |

Semantics are already right. The snapshot test in its code gives exactly the values it wrote, shifted by one column (cand_0002 confirmed this offline and the scorer agrees: 6 wrong cells + 5 empty cells). In the cand_0002 rollout, 43436 printed coordinate-keyed headers and PASSED. So the mechanism is confirmed by a measured RESULT (cand_0002 fixed={43436}).

## Building on cand_0002 (REJECTED, broke {267-18, 37456})
I read the cand_0002 rollouts of both broken tasks against the cand_0001 passing traces:
- **267-18 (G1:G2)**: under cand_0001 the agent printed `G1 None | was: '[...]'`, noticed that G1 had lost its formula's cached value, and wrote G1's literal → pass. Under cand_0002, its printout had no `was:` column, so it accepted `G1: None`, left G1 as a formula, and failed ("answer cells hold FORMULAS"). The cause is that cand_0002's new Phase 3 item told it a `None` in a cell it believed "already filled" meant **shifted letters**. That framing is wrong when the cell held a formula. In this run the same check names **both** causes and tells them apart with `was:`. On 267-18's trace (`was:` holds a value) it points to "write that value as a literal", which is exactly what the passing trace did.
- **37456 (G12:J15)**: under cand_0002 the agent built `summary_dates` from rows 12–15 only and skipped the last row ("Only run when a next date exists"). Under cand_0001 it read `ws.cell(r + 1, 6)` → pass. The cand_0002 Phase 1 recipe (coordinate-keyed rows over all columns, every task) changed its first-turn inspection. That is plausibly unrelated variance on a volatile task. Either way, I do **NOT** re-ship the global Phase-1 recipe change. The Phase 1 recipe is unchanged in this iteration.

## Changes made
| # | cluster | edit class (system-prompt SKILL menu) | file | what | blast radius |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | I | add sourced rule / worked idiom (KNOWLEDGE) | prompt.md §3 new conditional bullet | "**When you pick target columns by their header**…" Take letters from openpyxl `c.column_letter`, not from counting the preview or a positional list, plus a 2-line idiom that prints `[(letter, header)]`. | BOUNDED: it fires only when the agent maps headers to target columns. Passing tasks in that class (37456, 50768, 7902, 560-12, 142-12, 402-43) already map correctly. The idiom only adds letters to the same headers, and no decision rule changes. |
| E2 | I (+ guards the 267-18 case) | pre-finish checklist item (STRUCTURE) | task_template.md Phase 3 | A target cell believed already filled must not read `None`. If it does, `was:` tells the cause apart: `was: None` means shifted letters, so re-derive them; `was:` holds a value means a formula lost its cache, so write the literal. | BOUNDED: it fires only when a believed-filled target reads `None`. In the 37 passing traces this occurs only in 267-18 turn 5, where the new item prescribes the action the passing trace already took. |

The Phase 1 recipe, §2, Phase 1b and the CONTRACT are untouched. The edits are additive only.

## Verify-the-fix
- E1 — trace 43436 turn 2: `print("Headers:", [ws.cell(1, c).value for c in range(1, 12)])`, then the comments "Column I: Open as of today (already filled) / Column J: May / Column K: Jun". With E1, the idiom prints `('H','Open as of today'), ('I','Open by of end of May 2022'), …, ('K','Open by end of Jul 2022')`. The letters are read, so May→I, Jun→J, Jul→K, and its own snapshot code yields the expected values. Measured precedent: cand_0002 rollout 43436 printed coordinate-keyed headers, mapped H/I/J/K correctly and scored 1.0.
- E2 — trace 43436 turns 7/9/11/13/15: `Row 2: I=None, J=1, K=2`, with I believed already filled and `was: None` (original I2 is None). The new item names this and prescribes re-deriving the letters instead of re-sending the same block, so the 5 identical resubmissions would have become a re-map.
- E2 safety — trace 267-18 (cand_0001, passing) turn 5: `G1 None NoneType | was: '["/link/", ...'`. The new item routes this to "write that value as a literal", which matches turn 6 of the passing trace. This is the exact case cand_0002's one-cause wording mis-routed.
- Placeholders: `string.Formatter().parse` on the comment-stripped template gives exactly the 7 allowed fields.

## Process & features used
- Serial. There is one capability cluster, and CLAUDE.md forbids Agent/Workflow unless the user requests it.
- Read: LEDGER, JOURNAL, RUNMAP, prior_iterations/cand_0002 (PROCESS + diff), and the cand_0002 val rollouts of 43436/267-18/37456 against the cand_0001 traces.

## Preserve
- Phase 1 recipe as-is (the cand_0002 global recipe change co-occurred with the 37456 break).
- Everything in cand_0001's PRESERVE list (CONTRACT 1, to_excel allowed, Phase 3 stop rule, §2 conditional rules, no universal mandatory steps).

## Deliberately skipped
- Global coordinate-keyed Phase 1 recipe (cand_0002): co-occurred with the 37456 break, so it was dropped and replaced by the conditional §3 bullet.
- 227-40 / 45635: environment.
- No other failing clusters exist in this iteration's traces: 37/40 pass, 2 are env.

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate
